holidays.name: National Peanut Butter and Jelly Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the sticky, sweet, and salty sandwich that has rescued lunchboxes everywhere. Whether you are a crunchy or smooth devotee, grape or strawberry loyalist, today you pledge allegiance to the PB&J.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial American food holiday, popularized by food-observance calendars. The sandwich itself dates to the early 20th century, with an early recipe for a peanut butter and jelly sandwich appearing in 1901 in the Boston Cooking School Magazine. It later became a staple for U.S. soldiers in World War II.
holidays.funFact: The average American kid eats about 1,500 peanut butter and jelly sandwiches before graduating high school.

holidays.name: International Fact-Checking Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the noble art of questioning everything you read online, verifying sources, and resisting the urge to share that suspicious meme. It is a celebration of truth, receipts, and healthy skepticism.
holidays.origin: Launched in 2017 by the International Fact-Checking Network at the Poynter Institute. It was intentionally placed on April 2, right after April Fools' Day, as a sort of sober morning-after to a day of pranks and hoaxes.
holidays.funFact: It was scheduled the day after April Fools' Day on purpose, so the world can recover from the pranks and check what was actually true.

holidays.name: World Autism Awareness Day
holidays.description: A global day to promote understanding, acceptance, and inclusion of autistic people. Landmarks around the world light up in blue, and communities host events centered on neurodiversity.
holidays.origin: Designated by the United Nations General Assembly in 2007, with the first observance in 2008. It was proposed by Qatar and has since grown into a worldwide movement.
holidays.funFact: Many famous buildings, including the Empire State Building and the Sydney Opera House, have glowed blue for the occasion.

holidays.name: International Children's Book Day
holidays.description: A day for celebrating the magic of kids' books, from bedtime classics to wild picture books about talking vegetables. Libraries and schools hold readings and give out books to encourage young readers.
holidays.origin: Established in 1967 by the International Board on Books for Young People (IBBY). The date was chosen to honor the birthday of Hans Christian Andersen, born April 2, 1805, the Danish author of The Little Mermaid and The Ugly Duckling.
holidays.funFact: Each year a different national section of IBBY sponsors the day, and they pick a theme and have an artist design a poster for it.

holidays.name: National Ferret Day
holidays.description: A day to honor those long, wiggly, mischievous noodle-shaped furballs who steal socks and do the famous weasel war dance. Ferret fans celebrate with treats, playtime, and tunnel adventures.
holidays.origin: An unofficial pet holiday celebrated by ferret owners and fans in the United States, promoted by pet-themed observance calendars as a way to recognize ferrets as pets.
holidays.funFact: When ferrets get super excited, they perform the 'weasel war dance,' a frenzied series of sideways hops, bumps, and chattering sounds.
